text: Dov Halevi. I count out loud. People find it irritating, and I've decided not to stop.
You don't play. Then there's nothing for me to count. Wren teaches, down the steps.
A game? I'll count the whole way through, and you'll find it irritating.
A game nobody counts teaches nobody anything.

exit.intro: He sets his watch on the table beside the bowl and does not look at it once.

text: Then I'll count the machines. The one on the end is thirty seconds behind the rest.
Again. I'll count quieter. I won't, but I'll try.
You were ahead from move forty and played the rest as if you were behind.
That's the expensive habit. Not reading. Not knowing.
I said the number at move sixty, and it was the number at the end.
Nobody believes me until the end. That's why I do it out loud.
